x: With Brian Johnston and Trevor Hart backing up well and the ever improving Eric Penny securing sixth position, Woodford and Finchley were well and truly put behind.
Eric Penny, our fourth scorer, in his first year as a junior was plugging away steadily about fortieth, making headway in the typical "Penny" tradition.

After half a mile it looked as though our lads were going to repeat their Surrey performance with Ken and Alan in the first dozen, but after a further 2 miles Ken lay 23rd, with John Thresher and Ken Venton in the 80's and Eric Penny at 152nd ahead of Alan, who had dropped to 181.
After half-mile he, Alan Black and John Thresher were in the first 20, and with Ken Venton and Eric Penny only a little way behind— a most promising start.

In the Surrey County Junior Championships at Warlingham on January 13th, Chris Steer (8th) Tony Fairclough (10th), Eric Penny (28th) and Philip King (42nd) were placed 6th in the team race.

Chris Steer led our men home in 57th place, closely followed by Tony Fairclough. Eric Penny 127th and an under-trained Cyril Forey 178th completed our team. We shall do much better in this Championship in future years.

Tony Fairclough proved too strong for the other two youths and finished third, a minute behind the winner. Eric Penny and Philip King were two of several runners that went off course, but fortunately this did not affect the Championship result.

Chris Steer finished first for us but after his recent good form was rather disappointing, Eric Penny and Tony Fairclough battled gamely on, whilst Cyril Forey gave us ample proof of his lack of training.

Positions remained fairly static on the fourth stage with Eric Penny and Howerd Satchell recording the same times. Next off for the 'A' team was John Thresher who passed a struggling Clive Shippen (running for the 'B' team) to bring us up to 8th.

It was good to see Eric Penny back in action again and we hope to see more of him on the road. 'Glimpy' Jones is also enjoying a new lease of life at present and "out to get" the elusive Charlie Smart.
Eric Penny and Chris Keavey again continued to show an improvement, whilst Don Maclean found the course, the heat and achilles trouble a little too much for one afternoon.

Of our other runners, and we had 25 out all together, the bouquets went to Bob Glover and Eric Penny. Bob was showing some of his old fire again and moved very well to finish 96th, and Eric continued his steady improvement to record a best ever placing of 118th.
These three were followed home in quick succession by Eric Penny, Bernard Merry and John Hall who thus disproved the suggestion that Belgravians do not know how to 'pack' these days.

Up and coming Pat O'Connor put in another very strong run whilst Eric Penny took nearly two minutes off his last year's time. Finally Gordon bid welcome to Eric Penny and his wife Pat. Apart from his athletic career in Bel's colours, Eric was truly the lynch-pin of the famous Belgrave Skiffle Group set up by Bill Couzens back in 1973.
Eric Penny 1941-2009 Regrettably we must announce the passing of Eric Penny who died on 23 February aged 68.
